messages:
mike: FYI — after the RBAC tidy up this morning we're seeing inter-region mTLS failures. Errors point to KMS unwrap denies for session ticket keys in eu-west and ap-south.
leah: ugh. when did the roll happen? any canary / changelog link?
samira: Happened ~08:12 UTC. I pulled a sample proxy log: 
```
2026-03-21T08:17:23Z proxy-edge eu-west-1 ERROR tls: unwrap failed: KMSDecryptDenied: Access denied for key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111222333:key/abcd-ef01
principal=svc-keystore-rotator@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
mike: thanks. rbac-bot, can you show the policy diff for the rollout?
rbac-bot: policy-roll-#987 applied at 08:11 UTC. Diff (summary): removed binding keystore.unwraper -> svc-keystore-canary; added binding keystore.unwraper -> svc-keystore-main. Full diff: `- svc-keystore-canary, + svc-keystore-main`
jordan: did the rotator service identity change from `svc-keystore-main` to `svc-keystore-canary` or vice-versa?
samira: Canary was *supposed* to be bound, but the automation flipped the binding during a prune. So the rotating instances in eu-west/ap-south still present identity `svc-keystore-canary` and lost permission.
leah: can we temp rebind the key to the canary principal to restore traffic while we fix policy?
mike: yes — quick mitigation: add back unwrap permission for svc-keystore-canary on the affected KMS keys, then roll the canary to pick up new creds.
samira: patch command I ran in test: 
```
# AWS example
aws kms put-key-policy --key-id abcdef01 --policy file://policy-add-canary.json
# gcp example (if using CMEK key ring):
 gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding abcdef --location=global --keyring=prod-kr --member=serviceAccount:svc-keystore-canary@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```
jordan: also we need better audit log context — add principal + key id to the alert and log aggregation so we can match deny -> change quickly.
leah: Agreed. New rule: when KMS decrypt DENY occurs, include `requestContext.principal`, `keyId`, and `rbac-change-id` if present. Samira can you add a short patch to the log forwarder?
samira: on it. planning to inject this filter into logstash: `if [error] =~ /KMSDecryptDenied/ { add_field => { "kms_principal" => "%{[requestContext][principal]}" } }`
mike: long-term: we should make key unwrap permission additive for a rolling window when we flip keystore principals (30m overlap). Add to runbook.
leah: +1. Also add an automated smoke check that runs after RBAC changes: `curl https://proxy-health.eu-west/ping --header "x-keystore-test: unwrap"` and verify 200/unwrap success in logs.
oncall-bot: incident created: INC-20260321-91 — priority P2. Assigned: samira, jordan. Timeout: 1h.
jordan: Action list: 1) Mitigate by re-binding canary to affected keys (samira) 2) Patch log forwarder to include principal/keyId (samira) 3) Add canary overlap policy to RBAC playbook (mike) 4) Add smoke check to post-RBAC CI (leah)
leah: I'm going to add the smoke check PR now.
samira: Mitigation applied in eu-west and ap-south at 08:33 UTC. I'm seeing unwrap success in proxy logs already. Sample: 
```
2026-03-21T08:34:05Z proxy-edge eu-west-1 INFO tls: unwrap OK key=abcdef01 principal=svc-keystore-canary
```
mike: Nice. Jordan — can you follow up on the automation rule that pruned the canary binding? We need to avoid destructive prune when multiple identities exist across regions.
jordan: will do. Proposing we add region-scoped safe-check and an explicit `--force` flag for destructive prune.
leah: closing loop: once smoke checks are green for 15m, demote incident to postmortem and file a vuln triage for the RBAC automation and attach diff snapshot.
mike: thanks all. Postmortem owners: samira (mitigation + logs), jordan (automation fix), leah (smoke checks). I'll ping infra to schedule a brief review. :thumbsup:
